_comment: 🧩️ DOCX ECMA-376/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform -- its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). A DOCX is a ZIP of XML parts, and both `zip` 6 and `quick-xml` 0.42 are already linked and are genuinely independent of this repository's own codec: `zip` unzips/rezips the OPC container, `quick-xml` parses/edits/re-serializes the OOXML parts (word/document.xml, word/styles.xml, [Content_Types].xml, every *.rels). Registered as ONE oracle entry naming the composition -- neither library alone reads a DOCX; the pair together is the real independent implementation, and this subset's own oracle module (../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs) is the composition code, not a third dependency.

oracles.rationale: A DOCX is ECMA-376 WordprocessingML: an OPC package (a real ZIP archive) of real XML parts. `zip` is the reference ZIP reader/writer, used here to unzip and rezip the container; `quick-xml` is the reference XML reader/writer, used here to parse and re-serialize word/document.xml, word/styles.xml, [Content_Types].xml and every *.rels part. Composed, they read and write a genuine DOCX end to end, independently of `crate::artifacts::docx`/`crate::artifacts::zip::opc` -- this oracle module never imports `semio-s-plugin-stdio` and reimplements the OPC/WordprocessingML layer itself against the two reference libraries directly. Registered under its own id/capability, distinct from the neighbouring `xml-1-0-mutate` (📰xml/ecma-376's own quick-xml registration) and `zip-2-0-mutate` (🎒️zip/2.0's own zip registration): reusing either would fail the contract's oracle-capability-mismatch check, and a mutation vocabulary belongs to the subset that declares it.

comparisonProfiles.description: DOCX documents compared by the typed semantic view this subset's own `DocxDocument` models: `body` (the ordered w:body block tree -- paragraphs with their style reference and ordered runs, tables with their ordered rows/cells, recursively) and `styles` (the ordered w:styles list, id/name/basedOn), both order-sensitive per WordprocessingML's own document-order semantics. Every OTHER real OPC part (docProps/*, any part touched only through SetPart/RemovePart) is compared by content-type plus content digest, projected as an unordered path-keyed map so writer-freedom part ORDER never registers as a difference. word/document.xml and word/styles.xml themselves are excluded from that raw-part map: two independent writers legitimately differ byte-for-byte on non-semantic whitespace/attribute-order/self-closing-form for the exact same document, which is exactly why the typed body/styles projection exists instead. [Content_Types].xml and every *.rels part are pure OPC plumbing, regenerated deterministically from the typed content-types/relationships tables on every re-encode by both sides, and are not part of the comparison at all -- neither side's typed mutation vocabulary (13 kinds: NoMutation, SetSnapshot, InsertBlock, RemoveBlock, SetBlockContent, SetRunText, SetRunFormatting, InsertStyle, RemoveStyle, SetStyleName, SetStyleBasedOn, SetPart, RemovePart) ever targets them directly.
